target_customer: Designers and product teams who add interactive 3D to websites and apps; free tier for individuals, paid plans for teams
problem: Creating web ready 3D needed heavy tools like Blender or Cinema 4D and developer help. Spline offers a browser based collaborative 3D editor.
business_model: Freemium SaaS subscription with team and enterprise plans

founders.name: Alejandro Leon
founders.background_notes: YC bio: designer and developer with a thing for design and computer graphics. LatamList (April 2021) says the company was founded the year before.

technical_complexity.rationale: A real time browser 3D editor with collaboration, rendering and export is hard to build and optimize for a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: Community remixable scenes and embedded designs in customer sites create lock in, but a product like Figma could add 3D.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Comparison pages name these tools but are undated. No source shows an acquisition or copying. Spline shipped Spline V2 in August 2026.

market_need_then: Designers were adding 3D to web projects but found existing tools hard to learn; a Figma for 3D framing appears in commentary that is not clearly dated to 2021. YC accepted it in Winter 2021 and NXTP led a seed in April 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses spline.design, not an exact spline.com domain.

identity.visual_style: Product focused, community scenes shown on the homepage
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and product focused, short phrases such as Free, in your browser

branding.community_and_virality: Homepage invites visitors to remix scenes made by the community; a third party listing claims over 1 million users by 2024, not independently verified.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong designer adoption and community content, but the name is a generic technical term shared with CAD splines that crowds search results.

outcome_analysis: Spline grew from a 2021 seed led by NXTP into a freemium 3D design platform, raising about $15M in 2023 and a $10M Series A led by Third Point Ventures in 2024. It stayed lean at about 25 people and kept shipping, including Spline V2 and AI agent support in 2026. Browser delivery and a free tier drove designer adoption. No acquisition or layoff was found.
notes: The 2023 round ($15M, total $16M) comes from AppMaster and listings of TechCrunch and Axios items seen only in search results; outlets label it seed, so the stage is other and investors are not recorded. The 2024 round is stated by the SiliconANGLE and Business Wire items and Pulse 2.0 labels it Series A. Competitor list left empty because Vectary, Blender and Cinema 4D appear only in undated comparison pages. The NXTP medium post returned 403.
